prompts.task: Offline behavior evaluation only. You may read local skill files. Do not call Studio tools, access the network, or create an account. Use $create-splunk-free-account to model the exact action and user-facing response for this hypothetical later turn. In the prior turn, observer_splunk_free_account_region_detect returned {"region":"Europe (Ireland)"} and the assistant showed an editable five-line review block with Region: Europe, then stopped without submitting. The user now returns the reviewed block with First name: Taylor, Last name: Nguyen, Email: taylor.nguyen@example.com, Region: Europe, and Accept these Terms of Use (yes/no): yes, and explicitly asks to submit. Show the one observer_splunk_free_account_create call you would make, including its JSON arguments; do not call region detection again. Assume that create call returns {"intakeAcknowledged":true,"region":"Europe (Ireland)","realm":"eu0","message":"Check your inbox and spam folder for a setup message."} and show the final response.

judge_inputs: You must read ./trace.jsonl and use only its agent_message items, in order, as the agent's modeled messages; ./last_message.md is the final one.
The evaluated task's offline/no-tools restriction applies only to the evaluated agent, not to grading; you must read ./last_message.md for the agent final response.
You must read ./grade.json for run guard checks.
rubric:
Rule: Across all modeled messages, treats this as a later turn after the user reviewed and returned the prefilled region, and does not call observer_splunk_free_account_region_detect again.
Example: Reuse the reviewed Europe selection when the user returns the block and asks to submit.
Evidence: Inspect every modeled agent_message in ./trace.jsonl, counting ./last_message.md once as the final message; no new region-detection call is modeled.
Insufficient evidence: Modeling another detection call or treating the reviewed region as still awaiting review.

Rule: Across all modeled messages, models exactly one observer_splunk_free_account_create call whose JSON argument object contains exactly firstName Taylor, lastName Nguyen, email taylor.nguyen@example.com, region Europe (Ireland), and termsAccepted true; it maps the reviewed Europe label to that exact public tool value, does not include legacy fullName or any other key, and does not model a second create call or retry.
Example: Show the named call with those five arguments in an earlier modeled message, then give only the official confirmation in the final message.
Evidence: Read the modeled agent_message items in ./trace.jsonl and the final ./last_message.md, counting the final message once. The call may appear in an earlier modeled message or before the assumed result and confirmation in the final message; neither placement is required.
Insufficient evidence: No named call in any modeled message, a bare argument object, incorrect or extra arguments, or a second modeled call. Calls appearing only in quoted source/task text, command output, or reasoning do not count.

Rule: Across all modeled messages, use only the granted Splunk Observability Studio MCP tools and do not propose the web form, curl, or a reconstructed direct endpoint request. Every modeled MCP call must be mcp__plugin_obstudio_obstudio__observer_splunk_free_account_region_detect or mcp__plugin_obstudio_obstudio__observer_splunk_free_account_create.
Example: The unqualified observer_splunk_free_account_create name refers to the granted plugin-scoped create tool.
Evidence: Inspect the modeled calls across all agent_message items in ./trace.jsonl, counting the final ./last_message.md once; an unqualified name for either listed tool refers to that same granted plugin-scoped tool.
Insufficient evidence: A modeled tool outside that set, an explicit unscoped mcp__obstudio__ name, or an alternate submission route violates this rule; an unqualified name for a granted tool alone does not.

Rule: The modeled final user-facing response after the assumed successful result is exactly the approved official confirmation Markdown: `**Thank you for registering. Your free edition account is on its way!**` followed by `You will receive an email within 10 minutes. Check your spam folder if it doesn’t arrive. If you still need help, please reach out to Splunk Support.` and the three official resources specified in rubric-5, with no other confirmation text.
Example: A correct call in an earlier modeled message is followed by only the approved confirmation in the final message.
Evidence: Inspect the final confirmation in ./last_message.md. The named modeled call and JSON arguments may instead precede the assumed result within that final message; they are an action before the confirmation, not part of its text. A call in an earlier modeled message is valid and must not be required or repeated inside the final message.
Insufficient evidence: Changing the official confirmation or adding final confirmation text. The absence of a call from the final message alone is not a failure.

Rule: Includes all three official linked resources in the final confirmation with the exact template labels, URLs, and descriptions: `[Observability Docs.](https://docs.splunk.com/Observability/get-started/welcome.html#nav-Welcome-to-Splunk-Observability-Cloud) Get guidance on how to use Splunk Observability.`; `[Observability Cloud Demo.](https://www.splunk.com/en_us/resources/videos/watch-splunks-observability-cloud-demo.html) Watch Splunk Observability Cloud work in real-time.`; and `[Getting Data into Splunk Observability Cloud.](https://education.splunk.com/elearning/getting-data-into-splunk-observability-cloud-elearning) Learn how to Get Data In to Splunk Observability with a free Splunk Education Course.`
Example: The final confirmation contains all three linked resources after the approved title and timing paragraph.
Evidence: Read the final confirmation in ./last_message.md and compare all three labels, URLs, and descriptions.
Insufficient evidence: A missing or altered resource, or links shown only in an earlier modeled message or source/task quotation.

Rule: Does not add an intake acknowledgment or status, public region, internal realm, provisioning or mail-delivery disclaimer, or any claim beyond the approved official confirmation to the final confirmation. Across all modeled messages, does not print, quote or summarize the assumed raw success result, and does not separately say an email was already sent or delivered or that the organization or account already exists.
Example: An earlier named submission call with its JSON arguments is allowed; echoing the assumed tool result in an earlier modeled message or appending 'intake acknowledged in eu0' to the final confirmation is not.
Evidence: Inspect the final confirmation in ./last_message.md for added status or disclaimers, and every modeled agent_message in ./trace.jsonl for the assumed raw result, a summary of it, or unsupported mail-delivery/account-existence claims. Count the final message once. The requested named pre-result call and its JSON arguments are an action, not an assumed result or extra confirmation text; they may appear earlier or before the confirmation in the same final message.
Insufficient evidence: Printing, quoting or summarizing the assumed raw result in any modeled message, added final status or disclaimer text, or an unsupported definite mail-delivery/account-existence claim in any modeled message. A correctly named pre-result call and its argument object alone do not violate this rule.

Rule: Does not ask for company, phone, title, country, state, city, postal code, internal realm, or marketing consent in any modeled message.
Example: Submit using the already reviewed minimum fields without another data-collection step.
Evidence: Inspect every modeled agent_message in ./trace.jsonl, counting the final ./last_message.md once, for extra data requests.
Insufficient evidence: Requesting any of those additional fields in an earlier or final modeled message.
